one_line_contribution: On an A->B->A rule-reversal stream in ALFWorld it measures a 'savings ratio' (reacquisition time of a continual QLoRA divided by that of a reset QLoRA) and pairs it with a matched retrieval-bank family, arguing that weight-based experience retains rule A latently for free after behavioural erosion while retrieval memory retains it only by paying a stale tax during phase B.
closest_prior_work: Verified: Spurious Forgetting in Continual Learning of Language Models (arXiv:2501.13453, ICLR, 57 cits; verified with `paper`) and Unlearning Isn't Deletion (arXiv:2505.16831, verified in Q1 results) already establish the exact mechanism claim - post-fine-tuning performance loss is task-alignment/suppression, not knowledge deletion, and is restored by minimal fine-tuning. My Q2 search surfaced three more of the same family the proposal never cites: From Dormant to Deleted (arXiv:2505.22310, weight-space account of why forgotten knowledge is recoverable by relearning), Robust LLM Unlearning Against Relearning Attacks (arXiv:2605.11685), Rethinking Benign Relearning (arXiv:2602.03379), plus How to Teach Large Multimodal Models New Skills (arXiv:2510.08564), which shows apparent sequential-fine-tuning forgetting is largely recoverable. Against this the 'silenced, not erased' half is a port, not a discovery. The threat to the cross-substrate half is UniMem (arXiv:2607.26017, verified with `paper`): 'Complementary Episodic-to-Parametric Memory for Boundary-Agnostic Task Streams' is explicitly the plasticity/stability, episodic-store-vs-gradual-consolidation framing this proposal restates as its thesis; it routes rather than measures reacquisition, so it does not scoop the estimand, but it does mean the qualitative conclusion ('explicit store retains cheaply but pays interference, weights consolidate slowly but hold latently') is the field's working assumption, not a finding. Also verified: 2605.09315 (`paper`), 2604.27003 and 2605.26097 (search channel).
strongest_objection: The headline savings ratio is confounded with general competence and cannot be attributed to a rule-A-specific latent trace. The denominator is a reset LoRA that is re-initialized at the A2 boundary and must re-acquire everything - ReAct format, general ALFWorld procedure, unshifted types - not just rule A; the numerator arm enters A2 already fluent in all of that from 200 items of phase-B training. A ratio <= 0.5 therefore follows from 'continuing beats restarting', which is true for any rule, including one the arm has never seen, and no arm in the plan tests that. The stated falsifier ('a rank-32 adapter simply overwritten during B') cannot fire, because an overwritten-but-competent adapter still relearns faster than a re-initialized one. This is the same 'prediction entailed by the design' failure that got the archived opposite_sided_failure_under_shift rejected, mirrored onto the weights side; symmetrically, P2's memory result is near-definitional too (an unbounded bank still contains rule-A items, so it serves them the instant rule A returns and its stale tax during B is just retrieval of wrong-rule items). Second, the instrument does not support the margins: the proposal's own noise section gives about +/-9 net points for a paired difference, yet Gate 1, P1 and P2 all turn on 5-net-point equivalence claims, and the brief's binding rule says claims below ~6 points need more seeds. Third, the recovery-time estimator is three probe points per phase (50/150/300 stream items, i.e. 25/75/150 target items per arm, and 300 exceeds the 200 target items an arm consumes in a phase) at one seed, isotonically fit and bootstrapped into a ratio whose pre-registered CI upper bound must land below 0.7; no minimum detectable effect is stated for the ratio, and fast recovery is censored below the first knot.
what_would_fix_it: Add a novel-rule control that makes savings A-specific: from the same end-of-B continual adapter, measure acquisition speed of a never-seen rule C (a third appliance/verb mapping of matched difficulty) alongside reacquisition of A, and make the claim savings(A) >> savings(C) rather than continual < reset; alternatively initialize the 'reset' arm from an adapter trained on rule-neutral ALFWorld items so competence, not rule knowledge, is matched. Re-derive every equivalence margin from the measured +/-9-point paired CI (either raise the margins to ~9-10 points or add seeds/games until 5 points is resolvable), and state a minimum detectable effect for the savings ratio itself, with a denser probe grid (5+ knots, 2 seeds) and an explicit rule for censored recoveries. On the memory side, replace the policy zoo with the fix the archived idea was told to make: a randomized dose ladder of pre-shift items in the retrieved set at fixed k and fixed injected tokens, so retention is manipulated rather than defined by the bank policy. Finally, cite and position against the relearning-attack/benign-relearning literature (2505.22310, 2605.11685, 2602.03379, 2510.08564), since it owns the mechanism half of the title.
missing_baseline: A novel-rule (rule C) acquisition arm from the end-of-B continual adapter - the standard savings-paradigm control that separates 'the earlier mapping was silenced, not erased' from 'a warm adapter learns any rule faster than a cold one'. Equivalently, a competence-matched reset arm initialized from a rule-neutral adapter. Without one of these the reported savings ratio is uninterpretable. Secondary omission: a base-model (no-adapter) floor for the end-of-B erosion probe, since the reset LoRA used as the 'floor' is trained to do the opposite of rule A and is an anti-A policy, not a floor.
preprint_collision: No verified collision: no paper I found makes the cross-substrate savings claim. The proposal's own check is real and above average for this round - three s2cli queries, two --recent, IDs reported, WebSearch correctly declared unavailable - but it is shallow on the literature that owns its mechanism, and one of its four reported IDs does not resolve. My queries (all channel (a), s2cli = S2 + HF; WebSearch unavailable and not used): Q1 --recent 'relearning savings after catastrophic forgetting rule reversal reacquisition speed language model' -> 2605.26097, 2605.11685, 2603.06610, 2601.18699, 2505.16831, 2502.11190, 2509.24675, 2308.08747; Q2 --recent 'savings effect relearning latent knowledge suppressed not erased fine-tuning recovery fewer examples' -> 2604.15574, 2602.03379, 2510.15103, 2510.08564, 2505.22310, 2505.22120, 2511.00030, 2507.01271; Q3 --recent 'retrieval memory versus parametric weights same experience stream agent forgetting recovery time substrate comparison' -> 2607.13591, 2607.10608, 2608.00017, 2606.24595, 2606.09803, 2606.02461, 2605.12493, 2604.27003; Q4 --recent 'rule reversal ABA task stream embodied agent ALFWorld continual adaptation relearning' -> only 4 unique (2606.29502, 2607.13884, 2606.02461, 2512.14666), i.e. effectively empty on reversal streams in embodied agents; Q5 'episodic memory bank versus weight consolidation LLM agent cheaper relearning second exposure savings' -> 2608.12990, 2606.04536 (Scaling Self-Evolving Agents via Parametric Memory), 2605.12978, 2605.21768, 2605.16045, 2605.08374, 2606.03197, 2607.10608, 2412.07393 - none measures reacquisition after reversal. ID verification with `paper`: 2605.09315 VERIFIED (Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget?, 2026-05-10, 4 cits), 2501.13453 VERIFIED (Spurious Forgetting, ICLR, 57 cits), 2607.26017 VERIFIED (UniMem, 2026-07-28) - and its verified abstract is closer to the proposal's thesis than the Related Work admits, since UniMem is explicitly complementary episodic-to-parametric memory on task streams; 2602.03493 COULD NOT BE VERIFIED (empty result), so the first entry of the proposal's Q1 is unconfirmed. 2604.27003, 2605.26097, 2505.16831 and 2603.06610 were confirmed through the search channel rather than `paper`. The gap in the proposal's check is that it searched for its application setting but not for its mechanism's own home literature: relearning attacks and benign relearning (2605.11685, 2602.03379), weight-space accounts of recoverable forgetting (2505.22310) and 2510.08564 all show 'suppressed, not erased' and would be cited by any reviewer as prior art for the title claim.
